figures.title: Let the claim climb only as the evidence climbs
figures.desc: A four-stage evidence ladder from one observed run through repeated paired trials and pattern inspection to a conclusion bounded to the sampled conditions.
figures.caption: Move right only when the evidence named in the next plate exists; repeated observations widen the view, but they do not repair a weak metric or justify an unbounded claim.
figures.transcript: Stage one is one probe: report only what happened in that run. Stage two is repeated pairs: match version A and version B on the same input and conditions while balancing order. Stage three is pattern inspection: keep raw differences visible and inspect center, spread, direction, order, dependence, and exclusions. Stage four is a bounded claim: name the observed trials, conditions, uncertainty, and allowed decision. A bad acceptance test remains bad at every stage, and no number of reruns turns it into a valid measure.

items.label: BOUND THE CLAIM
items.detail: These trials · these conditions · this decision

figures.title: Pair the condition; interleave who goes first
figures.desc: A six-pair run plan that matches A and B within each pair and alternates first position so version and order are not assigned to the same column every time.
figures.caption: Read each marker as one matched pair in actual sequence; every pair is separate, order assignments interleave, and the calculated difference remains B minus A.
figures.transcript: Pair one runs A first and B second. Pair two runs B first and A second. Pair three runs A first and B second. Pair four runs B first and A second. Pair five runs A first and B second. Pair six runs B first and A second. Each pair keeps the same input, scoring rule, evaluator, and important nuisance conditions. The calculated quantity is always B minus A, regardless of run order. Interleaving the count-balanced order assignments prevents either assignment from occupying only the early or late pairs. It does not by itself prove independence or remove carryover; fresh state between pairs and an explicit reset record are still required.

figures.title: Read instability as a diagnosis surface
figures.desc: A diagnostic matrix mapping wide variance, order separation, trial dependence, and post-result exclusions to the check and next operator move each signal requires.
figures.caption: A noisy or asymmetric result is not dead data; use the row that matches the symptom to choose the next discriminating move and shrink the current claim.
figures.transcript: Wide spread calls for inspection of raw paired differences and nuisance conditions, followed by a smaller claim and another controlled probe if the decision requires it. An A-first versus B-first split calls for inspection of sequence and carryover, followed by a stronger reset and a predeclared count-balanced schedule interleaved or randomized across pair sequence. Repeated outputs that quote or inherit prior state reveal dependence; redefine a fresh trial boundary before counting more evidence. Exclusions invented after scores are visible signal cherry-picking; restore every run and apply only the predeclared rule. In every row, the immediate response is diagnosis and claim restraint, not automatic deployment or silent deletion.
